Thanks for the call today — good to connect. Quick recap from FinWise and what we need from Redwood to qualify performance for our integration:

- Business SLOs: P95 latency <= 300ms for standard text completion endpoints; for streaming chat we need first-chunk <= 150ms and sustained token streaming at ~30 tokens/sec.
- Throughput target: steady-state 50 requests/sec, spike up to 120 rps for 5m.
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent sessions (each session may stream responses).
- Test approach: FinWise will run a customer-led k6/Locust run in our staging environment using a mix of short and long prompts (we'll share scenarios).
- Needs from Redwood: k6 script template and guidance for streaming endpoints, a test API account (non-production) with usage tags, and an IP allowlist for our test runners.

Proposed test windows: Jul 15 09:00-11:00 PT or Jul 16 18:00-20:00 PT. We prefer Jul 15 morning if possible.

Can you confirm you can provide the test creds, k6 script, and IP ranges? Also let us know recommended warm-up/ramp schedule so we don't trigger cold-start noise.

Thanks,

Hi Sarah — quick technical clarifications and what we'll ship in the k6 template:

- Endpoints:
  - Standard completion: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions (JSON).
  - Streaming chat: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream (HTTP/1.1 chunked or SSE).

- Authentication: Bearer API key in Authorization header; the test account will be rate-limited to a soft cap we set for the test window to prevent production impact.

- Streaming guidance: k6 doesn't natively parse SSE; the template will demonstrate using a simple long-poll loop that counts first-byte latency and sustained tokens/sec by measuring response chunk timings. For higher fidelity you can run a small Locust worker that keeps an open HTTP connection.

- Ramp / warmup recommendation:
  - 10m low-traffic warm-up at 5 rps to populate caches (prefix/KV warm).
  - Linear ramp to target over 10m.
  - Hold at steady-state 50 rps for 30m, then spike test 120 rps for 5m.
  - For concurrency 200, run 50 VUs each maintaining 4 sessions (VUs approx = concurrency/4 depending on session behavior).

- Observability: please share the test run IDs and we'll correlate with our internal request logs. We'll enable a dedicated debug trace flag for your API key so we can capture detailed latency histograms without affecting other customers.

Attaching the initial k6 template and a small README.

[attachment: finwise_k6_script.js (text/javascript)]

Let me know if you need the streaming example in a separate Locust repo — happy to provide.

Thanks,
